parts.part: lambda_q (h5_kernel.py:75-82) sums signed w(k)*k^q over the symmetric lattice |j|<=116 and calls the result a certified upper bound on sup|K1^(q)|
parts.evidence: h5_kernel.py:57-59 builds ks=[j*h for j in -J..J] with J=int(ceil(30/(pi/12)))+1=116. ws=exp(-k^2/2). L79 tot=sum(wj*(kj**q)), with no abs(). L80 lam=tot/Z1.a+tail(q). The docstring at L76 reads 'Certified upper bound on sup_s |K1^{(q)}(s)| = (1/Z) sum w k^q'. My script found that the ks intervals are exact negatives of each other and the ws intervals are identical in pairs (sym_k=True, sym_w=True). So for odd q the signed sum is exactly 0 in exact arithmetic, and only rounding width is left.

parts.part: Mathematics: is there any reading under which the signed odd-q sum is a valid upper bound?
parts.evidence: No reading works. For odd q, K1^(q)(s)=±(1/Z)Σw k^q sin(ks). cov_exact.py:25 and :28 (archive member H2_foundations/cov_exact.py) say these are 'NONZERO SINE SUMS at s != 0'. The equality sup|K1^(q)|=(1/Z)Σw k^q holds only for even q: every term is then positive and the sup is reached at s=0. My script reproduces the even values exactly (15, 105, 945, 10395). A local per-box reading also fails. A box centred at t=0 with eta=0.0015 contains s=eta, where |K1^(7)(eta)|>=0.1575 (rigorous interval), compared with lambda_7.b=3.6e-39.

parts.part: tm_factor (L531-539) uses the Lagrange remainder in the right form, so lambda_q(n+TD+1) is exactly the quantity that must be an upper bound
parts.evidence: L535-537 sets the coefficients K1^(n+m)(t)/m! for m=0..TD. That is the degree-TD Taylor polynomial of K1^(n)(t+u). The exact remainder is K1^(n+TD+1)(xi)*u^(TD+1)/(TD+1)! with |u|<=eta. Bounding it needs sup|K1^(n+TD+1)| over the box, which the global sup also covers. L538 puts LAT.lambda_q(n+TD+1) in exactly that slot. The form is correct and the input to it is wrong. A valid input is (1/Z)Σw|k|^q + tail.

result.corrected_wording: The claim stands as written. Two small sharpenings: (1) The computed odd-q lambda_q at 40 digits is about 3.6e-39 for q=7, 3.0e-38 for q=9 and 2.9e-37 for q=11 (the lattice is built at 100 digits by cov_exact's import-time configure and summed at h5_run's 40 digits). (2) The true sup|K1^(7)| lies between 35.54 (rigorous lower bound at s=0.54) and 38.30 (the absolute sum), so 'of order Σw|k|^q/Z' is accurate. For even q, lambda_q is a valid and tight bound. The Lagrange remainder form in tm_factor is correct. The defect is only that L79 uses w*k^q where it should use w*|k|^q. At eta=0.0015 the factor remainder comes out about 1e-62 to 1e-58 where a valid bound would be about 1e-22 to 1e-18.
result.notes: The mathematics lens cannot refute the claim. The k -> -k symmetry makes the odd-q signed sum exactly 0, while K1^(q) for odd q is a nonzero sine sum (cov_exact.py:25,28). So no global or per-box reading makes lambda_q a valid bound for odd q. The Taylor polynomial at h5_kernel.py:535-537 is the standard degree-TD expansion, so the Lagrange remainder needs exactly sup|K1^(n+TD+1)|, which is the role L538 gives to lambda_q. My script is <SCRATCH>/covtrace/lens_notes/lamq/mathematics/lamq_check.py and its output is <SCRATCH>/covtrace/lens_notes/lamq/mathematics/lamq_check.out. The script imports nothing from the archive and I executed nothing from the archive or the extracted tree. The repo clone has no lambda_q (git grep on origin/main b7f72a71 finds nothing). Not assessed: whether the roughly 1e-22 of missing remainder changes any printed certified bound. It is probably negligible next to the other terms, but it is still a gap in the rigour of the certified path.

result.corrected_wording: The claim holds as written, with one magnitude detail made precise. In h5_kernel.py, Lattice.lambda_q (L75-82) adds up the signed terms w*k^q over the symmetric lattice (J = 116). For odd q this cancels to rounding level: at 40 digits, lambda_7 is about ±3.5e-39, lambda_9 about ±3e-38 and lambda_11 about ±3e-37. The true sup|K1^{(q)}| is 35.5, 288 and 2913 (|k|-sum bounds 38.3, 306 and 3064). tm_factor (L538) uses this value as the Taylor remainder, and no caller, cache, abs() or later check corrects it. The factor's remainder is therefore about 1e40 times too small whenever q = n+TD+1 is odd: odd n in StationBox (TD 5, L559) and even n in CoarseBox (TD 6, L1328). Such factors do occur: the Grr cross block produces f x fxx, which gives q = 9 and q = 7 under TD 6. They feed detgg_t, qnum_t, S2NUM and mu2NUM, which coarse_fine_hi evaluates on the certified cover in h5_run.py (L194-216) and the h5_run_r*.py drivers. In absolute terms the missing remainder is small: about 1e-22 to 1e-20 per factor at eta = 0.0015. This lens does not say whether any printed number moves.
result.notes:
I did not run anything from the archive. The numbers come from my own reimplementation of the L53-82 formulas: <SCRATCH>/covtrace/lens_notes/lamq/codepath/lamq_check.py (venv python3 -I -B).

On the "about 1e-38" figure: LAT is built when h5_kernel is imported (L112). The cov_exact import sets dps to 100 before that (cov_exact.py L71-72 and configure()), and h5_run sets dps to 40 afterwards (L25-26). So the lattice intervals are narrow, and the cancellation residue is set by the 40-digit arithmetic inside lambda_q: 3.5e-39 for q = 7, rising to 3e-37 for q = 11. If the lattice were built at 53 bits, the residue would be about 1e-13 instead, which still leaves the bound off by many orders of magnitude.

Out of scope for this lens: the absolute omitted error is tiny, about 1e-22 per factor at eta = 0.0015 and TD 6. In practice, the interval Horner overestimation on each sub-box in eval_box_sub and coarse_fine_hi may swamp it. That would not restore rigor, and whether any printed bound changes is UNKNOWN here. The claim itself makes no such statement.

StationBox (TD 5) is used only in the 'patches' lower-bound part (h5_run.py L470-500) and GBounds. The same defect hits odd-n factors there.

result.corrected_wording: The claim stands. One wording precision: CoarseBox encloses its TMs with TM.eval_box_sub (h5_kernel.py:294-312), which adds the same [-R.b, R.b] at L312 as eval_box does at L243. The finding is also not new. The 2026-09-17 records MATH-20260917-b9c2_H5_ANALYTIC_ADVANCE.md, MATH-20260917-b9c2_H5_LAMBDA_REPAIR.md and CLOSE-20260917-b9c2_H5_IMPACT_AND_REPAIR.md (at commit 7caac254, indexed from origin/main docs/public-math/sources-12.md) already identify the odd-q cancellation in the pinned kernel b2e6014c and trace it through CoarseBox and StationBox. result.notes: The records check does not refute the claim; it supports it. b2e6014c is the only h5_kernel version anywhere in the archive and is the one pinned by the H5 receipts and by CL-PIN-001 on main. No fixed version exists in the archive or in the origin/main tree. Records on other branches (2026-09-17, task b9c2) already document this exact defect and its CoarseBox (TD=6, q=n+7 for n=0,2,4) and StationBox consumers. They report that the old enclosures are disjoint from the true values at the driver's 40-digit precision, and they say no printed number has been shown false. Their reported old radius of about 1e-119 is from a 100-digit setup. At the run's 40 digits, my reproduction gives lambda_q(7) of about 2e-38, which matches the claim. The archived driver (19504b97) is pinned only as custody snapshot bytes.
